Consonant clusters are groups of two consonants or more together. They form a specific sound when they are combined in a particular way. Usually the sounds of some of the consonants may be reduced or dropped.
In -sts consonant clusters, the /t/ sound can be dropped.
In -sks consonant clusters, the /k/ sound can be dropped.

When you talk about lists, it is important to use the right stress and intonation. With lists, you raise the intonation for each word in a list until the last word in the list, which goes down.

images.text: Tom insists on lists. He basks in the glory of sanity. Whenever someone asks about one of his tasks, he tsks.  Tom boasts that when it comes to it, there are no risks. He posts his notes on the wall with post-its in varying shades of yellow, blue, pink and green to make his world vibrate with color. Even though you may think that  necessity is the mother of invention, sometimes it is not. Accidents often prove to be fruitful when it comes to inventions like the post-it notes that Tom loves so much. How else would he get through his day thinking, organizing and listing and posting?  Sticky notes are his friend!

Velcro, that buttonless fastener, was the brainchild of a Swiss engineer. He did tests with materials that were fashioned after the burdock disks that stuck to his socks and his dog's furry coat. He sat at his desk looking, drawing, considering options and trying out variations of the hook and loop fastener. Where would we be without velcro for tiny fists that have a hard time with buttons?

One of my favorite inventions is the simple toaster. It toasts my bread just the way I like it in the morning and if it breaks, a new one costs very little. I vary my routine with bagels, hot cross buns, pop-tarts and all types of bread. I never get tired of toast! Meet at tea time for crumpets! Let's end up with potato chips! Those salty, crispy, crunchy, thin slices of potatoes everyone loves so much! George Crum invented these in anger. Someone complained his potatoes weren't fried enough, so George  sliced the next batch super thin and fried them extra long. His customer loved them and begged for more. Ah inventions, don't you just love them!
